import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_52/training_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_52/training_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_52/training_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_52/training_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_52/training_4.csv"
]

# Read all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    dfs.append(df)

# According to operation_history, perform UNION of all source tables
# All source tables have the same schema:
# ['Time', 'Date', 'Room', 'Room_Capacity', 'Module', 'Registered_Students']

# Concatenate all dataframes vertically (union)
target_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Reorder columns to match target schema (which is the same as source schema)
target_columns = ['Module', 'Time', 'Date', 'Room', 'Room_Capacity', 'Registered_Students']
# The source columns order is different, so reorder accordingly
target_df = target_df[target_columns]

# Write the result to the target path
target_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_52/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source CSV files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_52/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_52/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_52/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
df3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_52/training_3.csv", index_col=0)
df4 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_52/training_4.csv", index_col=0)

# Join all source tables on the shared key columns: Time, Date, Room, Module
# Since all tables have the same schema, we join them pairwise on these columns
# We will do a chain of merges with inner join to keep only matching rows

df01 = pd.merge(df0, df1, on=['Time', 'Date', 'Room', 'Module'], how='inner', suffixes=('_0', '_1'))
df012 = pd.merge(df01, df2, on=['Time', 'Date', 'Room', 'Module'], how='inner')
df0123 = pd.merge(df012, df3, on=['Time', 'Date', 'Room', 'Module'], how='inner', suffixes=('_2', '_3'))
df_all = pd.merge(df0123, df4, on=['Time', 'Date', 'Room', 'Module'], how='inner')

# After join, columns from different tables are suffixed or duplicated.
# We need to sum Room_Capacity and Registered_Students from all tables.

# Collect all Room_Capacity columns
room_capacity_cols = [col for col in df_all.columns if 'Room_Capacity' in col]
# Collect all Registered_Students columns
registered_students_cols = [col for col in df_all.columns if 'Registered_Students' in col]

# Sum across these columns row-wise
df_all['Room_Capacity'] = df_all[room_capacity_cols].sum(axis=1)
df_all['Registered_Students'] = df_all[registered_students_cols].sum(axis=1)

# Select the final columns as per target schema order
final_cols = ['Module', 'Time', 'Date', 'Room', 'Room_Capacity', 'Registered_Students']
df_final = df_all[final_cols]

# Group by the leftmost columns that are string or int and unique in target examples
# Here, group by Module, Time, Date, Room and aggregate sums of Room_Capacity and Registered_Students
df_final = df_final.groupby(['Module', 'Time', 'Date', 'Room'], dropna=False, as_index=False).agg({
    'Room_Capacity': 'sum',
    'Registered_Students': 'sum'
})

# Write the final output CSV
df_final.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_52/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
